issue.title: pan handoff has no --project: an isolated --cwd lands every successor outside all registered projects (conv 1827)
acceptanceCriteria: `pan handoff` accepts `--project <key>` and records it on the successor conversation, so the successor groups under that project regardless of where its `--cwd` points. Accept either the projects.yaml key or the display name, matching how `POST /api/conversations` already resolves `projectKey` (`resolveProjectCwd`, `src/lib/overdeck/conversation-runtime.ts:867`) — unknown project is a clear non-ze

When `--project` is omitted, the successor **inherits the source conversation's project** rather than re-deriving from its own cwd. A handoff from a MYN conversation is MYN work even when it runs in an isolated worktree; today that inheritance doesn't happen at all.
The dashboard Fork/Handoff modal exposes the same choice, defaulted to the source conversation's project.

Project association is stored explicitly (a `projectKey`/`workspace_id` association on the conversation row), not re-derived from `cwd` at read time — otherwise the containment test keeps overriding it. Decide and document how this interacts with PAN-1577's proposed explicit override column; these two should land on **one** mechanism, not two.
Grouping honours the explicit association first and falls back to cwd containment only when it's absent, so existing rows keep working.
**Data cleanup:** reassign conv 1827 (`20260801-2fc7`) to the MYN project — its work is MYN registration + MIN-930/MIN-931 planning. Do it through the write door.
Docs: `pan handoff` reference page and the `pan-handoff` skill both document `--project`, its default (inherit from source), and the interaction with `--cwd`.

Regression tests: a handoff with an isolated `--cwd` outside every registered project still groups under the source's project; an explicit `--project` wins over both; an unknown `--project` fails loudly.
